concept.title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography: Weil Pairing and BLS Signatures
concept.concept_description: Formalize the Weil pairing on an elliptic curve and prove its bilinearity. Show that the BLS signature scheme is existentially unforgeable under the computational Diffie-Hellman assumption in the pairing group. Prove that the pairing allows short aggregate signatures.

concept.title: Girth-Expansion Equivalence for Optimal Small-Set Expanders
concept.concept_description: A left-regular bipartite graph of degree d is an s-optimal small-set expander (i.e., every subset X of left vertices of size t ≤ s has exactly d * t distinct neighbors, maximizing expansion) if and only if its girth is at least 2s + 2. This bridges the combinatorial property of girth with the expansion parameter α_G(t) and the optimality of the associated code B(G).
concept.mathematical_framing: A left-regular bipartite graph of degree d is an s-optimal small-set expander (i.e., every subset X of left vertices of size t ≤ s has exactly d * t distinct neighbors, maximizing expansion) if and only if its girth is at least 2s + 2. This bridges the combinatorial property of girth with the expansion parameter α_G(t) and the optimality of the associated code B(G).
concept.lean_guess: The forward direction assumes a cycle of length 2k ≤ 2s and shows that the k left vertices on the cycle must share neighbors, reducing the neighborhood size below dk and violating optimality. The backward direction assumes a subset X of left vertices of size t ≤ s with shared neighbors and constructs a cycle of length ≤ 2s, contradicting the girth assumption.
